title: GitHub App token minting (actions/create-github-app-token in workflows): require literal owner and repositories inputs, enforced by policy.rego deny rule
answers: Why does the policy check fail with 'must set a non-empty with.repositories' on my workflow's GitHub App token step?
How do I narrow the GitHub App installation token to only mlflow and internal repos in a workflow?
Where is the rule that stops create-github-app-token steps from having no owner or repository scope?
Why must I write repositories: mlflow instead of using github.repository for the App token?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope walks every workflow job (input.jobs, via job_steps) and checks each step whose uses starts with actions/create-github-app-token@ (client-id/private-key token minting, e.g. autoformat, copilot-agent, uv, ui-review, nailaopus workflows).
Rule: Every such step must set non-empty literal values for both with.owner and with.repositories; a blank or missing value produces a Conftest denial naming the job id and the missing key. Use bare repository names (repositories: mlflow, or a comma list such as mlflow,internal), not ${{ github.repository }}, which expands to mlflow/mlflow and matches nothing.
Symptom: A workflow's App token step without owner/repositories was rejected by the policy check (the token would otherwise be issued without an explicit repository narrowing).
Constraints: Covers only steps the rule's job_steps traversal sees in workflow jobs, as written in the diff; it does not check the permission-* inputs (a separate deny rule covers permissions). Applies to the create-github-app-token action only.
applies: Workflow YAML under .github/workflows that mints GitHub App tokens with actions/create-github-app-token, checked by Conftest with .github/policy.rego.
says: Automated policy check rejects pull request for missing target repository restrictions on application credentials.
Continuous integration compliance check fails because token generation lacks explicit repository scope.
Restrict generated application tokens to specific repositories to pass automated security checks.
Why did the security gate fail on application token creation in my workflow?
search: Workflow steps using `actions/create-github-app-token@` must specify non-empty literal values for both `with.owner` and `with.repositories`, enforced by `deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope` in `.github/policy.rego` via Conftest. Repositories must be bare names (e.g. `repositories: mlflow` or `mlflow,internal`) rather than `${{ github.repository }}` which expands to `mlflow/mlflow` and matches nothing. This policy check inspects `input.jobs` via `job_steps` in `.github/workflows` (such as autoformat, copilot-agent, uv, ui-review, and nailaopus), but does not validate `permission-*` inputs.
